_doc: THE MANAGER RUNS THE MERGE QUEUE. This file is the order, and it is manager state of record -- a cold successor reads it to know who is at the front and who is holding. Operator directive 2026-09-03, verbatim: 'your job is to manage the PR so that they're not competing with each other. You make the queue. You tell the one to rebase. You tell them when to do CI and merge.' ⚠️ THE RULE THAT MAKES A QUEUE A QUEUE: ONLY POSITION 1 REBASES. Everyone else HOLDS -- no rebase, no CI run, no merge attempt. A session that rebases while not at the front burns a ~16-minute pytest-run against a target that is about to move, and its result is void the moment position 1 lands. On 2026-09-03 every session rebased simultaneously against a main that moved 26 times, 19 of them on shared registers; #10918 was conflicted three times and #10923 the instant it went green.
main_hold_note: The manager branch's auto-merge is DISARMED (.github/pr-automerge-requests/workflow-overhaul-scope-z4sjm3.txt deleted). Manager state is still committed and pushed every sweep; it batches instead of landing. ⚠️ DO NOT RE-ARM while this queue is non-empty -- re-arming is what kept main moving under every sibling.

queue.owner: session_017DxuurbMW5ex5Q1f7xATqW (MI-95) — IDLE, so the manager is driving it
queue.note: MI-102, the canonization PR. Manager merged main in (249ff8da, 13:3xZ) because its author is idle and the conflict was register-only, which GitHub cannot resolve at all. guards + pytest-collect + repo-inventory GREEN at 13:35Z; pytest-run started 13:33:03Z (~16 min). Declares landing: hold, so MERGE BY HAND on green — never auto-merge.

PROMOTED 13:4xZ on merit, not as a queue filler. It converts an UNVERIFIABLE row into a verifiable one: OI-20260902-PER-MERGE-PING has never been observed, and measured again at 13:33Z the reason IS the defect this PR fixes — notify_on_pull logged `Queued 2 ping(s)` with no source named, so a healthy run is indistinguishable from one that never fired. Manager did three things it could not do for itself: merged main in (5244dafb; the only conflict was the GENERATED CLAUDE.md brief, re-rendered rather than hand-merged), WROTE ITS MISSING LANDING DECLARATION (it had none, so R11 would have failed it whatever its tier), and UN-DRAFTED it (a draft is a hold its own author cannot lift — sub-sessions 403 on update_pull_request).

The manager branch goes LAST and only once the queue is otherwise empty. Auto-merge stays DISARMED. Its landing declaration reads hold/depends_on_unmerged_pr #10920 with the imperfection disclosed — see MI-104: the vocabulary has no term for queue serialisation.

promotion_protocol: 2. Manager removes it from the queue and marks the NEW position 1 as REBASE_NOW.
3. Manager POKES that owner session -- a session does not poll this file, and an unpoked session is an idle session.
4. Only then does that session rebase and let CI run.
⚠️ A session that finishes work while HOLDING should push its branch and STOP. Pushing is cheap; rebasing and re-running CI is what is wasteful.
open_question_10398: STATUS 2026-09-03T11:00Z: STILL UNANSWERED, and the manager's own probe produced a FALSE VERDICT it caught before reporting. The question: does PRE-guard #10398 (branch automation/econ-calendar-33232352515-1) fail pr-landing R11? If a branch cut BEFORE the guard existed still fails, the 'could this branch have known' test does not do what its docstring claims. ⚠️ IT CANNOT BE ANSWERED FROM #10398's EXISTING CHECK RUNS: they are from 2026-08-29T03:50Z, five days before check_pr_landing.py was added to main (832523d0, 2026-09-03T09:35Z). Its `guards` failure is therefore NOT an R11 failure -- it predates the guard entirely, and its pytest-run failed too. Reading that red as an R11 verdict would be exactly the unprovenanced-diagnostic class. ⚠️ AND IT CANNOT BE ANSWERED FROM THIS CONTAINER: the clone is SHALLOW (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` -> true, .git/shallow present, only 75 commits reachable on main), so `git merge-base origin/main <branch>` returns EMPTY. A probe run here printed 'R11 MUST GRANDFATHER' -- but that came from `git merge-base --is-ancestor` failing on an EMPTY argument, not from a comparison. That is 'we did not look' rendering as a verdict, and it was discarded rather than reported. ✅ WHAT WAS ESTABLISHED: R11 IS RELIABLE IN CI. .github/workflows/guards.yml checks out with `fetch-depth: 0`, so the guard has full history there and its base comparison is sound. The shallowness is a limitation of the manager's container, NOT of the guard -- do not file R11 as broken on the strength of a local probe. THE ONLY WAY TO ANSWER IT: re-run #10398's checks against current main. Note it has been red and stalled ~113h with its own failing pytest-run, so a re-run answers the R11 question and does NOT make it mergeable.

cadence_incident: ⚠️ 2026-09-03T11:04Z: the manager's sweep timer (trig_016Tn8Kt9sDtQHhxG9NKQabT) stayed `enabled` with `next_run_at` in the PAST and NEVER FIRED. #10923 was green and mergeable from 11:01:05Z and sat until 11:11Z; the OPERATOR surfaced it, not the mechanism. MITIGATION: sweeps are now a REDUNDANT PAIR (~4 min and ~7 min) so one miss opens no gap. ⚠️ THAT IS REDUNDANCY, NOT A DETECTOR -- a send_later that does not deliver raises no error and changes no state the session can see, so a miss is indistinguishable from a manager choosing to do nothing. Filed as BL-20260903-MANAGER-CADENCE-RIDES-A-SINGLE-UNMONITORED-TIMER-THAT-SILENTLY-DID-NOT-FIRE and routed to MI-102 as the worked example for its duty-2 check: measure OBSERVED gaps between manager ACTIONS, never scheduled ones.
automation_batch_finding: ⚠️ MEASURED 2026-09-03T11:25Z, BEFORE the queue reached this batch: **#10923's fix is FORWARD-LOOKING ONLY and does NOT unlock the already-open automation PRs.** The fix makes `.github/actions/commit-to-main` WRITE the declaration as part of the commit it makes (verified: 3 pr-landing references in action.yml on main). But branches created BEFORE that merged carry no declaration of their own -- checked directly on automation/work-digest-33742749108-1 and automation/reconcile-open-prs-33742749146-1: both carry OTHER PRs' declaration files inherited from main, and NEITHER has `.github/pr-landing/<its-own-slug>.json`. So a re-run still fails R11. #10923's body says it 'unlocks 7 of the 7 currently-locked PRs' -- that is true of the MECHANISM going forward and NOT of those seven PR objects, and the distinction was not drawn. Do not read the merge as having freed them. DISPOSITION: these families REGENERATE on their own cadence (work-digest, reconcile-open-prs, probes, due-list, session-reaper, strategy-reviews), so the cheapest correct move is to CLOSE the stale ones and let the next run produce a compliant replacement -- which also clears the 3-deep duplicate stacking in one action. ⚠️ TWO EXCEPTIONS, do not close blindly: (a) **#10398** is econ-calendar POINT-IN-TIME snapshots, 5 days old, and PIT data does not necessarily regenerate identically -- closing it may DISCARD a snapshot, and it also carries its own failing pytest-run, so it needs a separate decision, not a batch close. (b) a work-digest PR carries a QUEUED PING in pending-pings.jsonl; closing it means that digest is never committed and the operator never receives it. Those digests are hours old and superseded by newer ones, so closing is right -- but say so rather than discarding silently.
stranded_ping_note: ⚠️ SELF-INFLICTED AND WORTH WATCHING: the F6 rolled-up digest this manager queued at 10:11:51Z lives in `docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl` ON THE MANAGER BRANCH, whose auto-merge is deliberately DISARMED. So it is queued and will NOT reach the operator until this branch merges. work_digest's own output warns 'COMMIT pending-pings.jsonl or the digest never happened (transit fails back, by design)' -- it is committed, but not to main. Holding main still to unjam the queue has this cost; it is accepted and recorded, not hidden.
how_the_manager_PINGS_the_operator_while: ⚠️ ESTABLISHED 2026-09-03T11:58Z, BEFORE it was needed, because the obvious path is BROKEN BY THE MANAGER'S OWN DECISION. The normal ping route is `docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl` -> committed to MAIN -> drained by ict-git-sync's notify_on_pull. But the manager branch's auto-merge is DISARMED to hold main still, so a ping queued that way NEVER REACHES THE OPERATOR until the branch merges -- the F6 digest queued 10:11:51Z is sitting there right now proving it. THE WORKING PATH IS THE `send-ping` SYSTEM-ACTION (allowlisted in .github/workflows/system-actions.yml, dispatched by a labelled issue). It enqueues DIRECTLY on the VM and bypasses the repo entirely, so it is unaffected by the branch freeze. ⚠️ AND ITS OWN SOURCE CARRIES THE TRAP, READ IT BEFORE CLAIMING A SEND: scripts/ops/send_ping_action.sh says 'EXIT 0 IS NOT ENOUGH TO CLAIM A SEND. A suppressed class-ping also exits 0' -- the class limiter can WITHHOLD a ping and still exit cleanly, logging `withheld: <reason>`. So READ THE OUTCOME, never the exit code. ⚠️ AND PREFER THE PASSTHROUGH SHAPE (leave `kind` blank) FOR ANYTHING THE OPERATOR IS ACTUALLY WAITING ON: the three classes (decision | state_change | lifecycle) are RATE-LIMITED by design, so a class ping is the one that can be silently withheld. A ping the operator is blocked on must not ride the channel most likely to be suppressed.
restart_owed_on_10916: ⚠️ THE SECOND HALF OF THE OPERATOR'S APPROVAL IS OUTSTANDING: restart `ict-claude-decision-bot.service` so the new startup path runs. FINDING WHILE LOOKING FOR THE ROUTE: **there is NO allowlisted system-action that restarts THIS unit.** `restart-bot-service` hardcodes `UNIT="ict-trader-live.service"` (scripts/ops/restart_bot.sh:26) -- it cannot target the decision bot. The only allowlisted lever that would reach it is `pull-and-deploy`, which refreshes units and restarts ~14 of them; that is a much wider blast radius than the operator approved for a menu fix. CHOSEN ROUTE: let ict-git-sync do it. It pulls every ~5 min and DOES deploy+restart on a real sha change -- observed today at 08:00:46Z when ClaudeBot restarted after #10904 landed, and its own log distinguishes 'Running processes already deployed at <sha>; nothing to deploy' from a real deploy. #10916 merged ~12:00Z, so the next pull should carry it. THEN VERIFY, IN THIS ORDER: (1) /api/diag/version shows the new sha deployed; (2) /api/diag/journalctl?unit=ict-claude-decision-bot.service carries the line `menu button was <X>, now 'commands'` -- ⚠️ IF <X> IS `web_app` THAT WAS THE CAUSE AND THE LOG SAYS SO, which is the whole point of the read-back; (3) ONLY THEN ask the operator to tap the Menu button. ⚠️ IF THE MENU IS STILL EMPTY after a confirmed restart, the remaining candidate is CLIENT-SIDE CACHING, which no code change can fix -- and the read-back will have ruled the other two out by then. Do not re-fix it blind.
MI_96_CAUSE_FOUND:
✅ #10916 DEPLOYED AND THE READ-BACK NAMED THE CAUSE. /api/diag/version: git_sha 56e8469d == git_sha_on_disk, restart_pending false. ict-claude-decision-bot restarted 12:05:58Z. THE LOG LINE, verbatim:
  `published /start, /status, /decisions; BEFORE default=['start', 'status', 'decisions'] all_private_chats=['atart']; telegram now returns ['/start', '/status', '/decisions'] for all_private_chats`
⚠️ THE CAUSE IS `all_private_chats=['atart']` -- A TYPO'D COMMAND NAME. Per the Bot API resolution chain (chat -> all_private_chats -> default, FIRST NON-EMPTY WINS), that single corrupt entry in the MORE SPECIFIC scope SHADOWED the default scope, which had the correct ['start','status','decisions'] all along. The commands were published correctly and were being outranked by one misspelled word.
⚠️ NOTE WHAT THIS DOES TO THE PR'S OWN REASONING, because it is the more useful half: #10916 named the MENU BUTTON as its 'best-supported candidate'. THE READ-BACK REFUTED IT -- `menu button was 'commands', now 'commands'`, so it was never a web_app button. What actually fixed it was the write the author called 'DEFENSIVE, NOT A DIAGNOSIS' -- the all_private_chats write they kept after correcting their own fabricated justification for it mid-PR. THE LEADING THEORY WAS WRONG AND THE HEDGE WAS RIGHT, and only the read-back could tell them apart. That is the whole argument for logging the branch nobody logs.
⚠️ STILL OPEN, do not close it silently: HOW DID 'atart' GET THERE? Nothing in this repo writes that string (the PR's own grep found ZERO prior setMyCommands calls for this bot), so it predates the repo's involvement -- most likely a hand-typed BotFather entry. Worth one grep of history and, failing that, recording as unexplained rather than assumed.
NEXT: the operator taps the Menu button. If it now lists the three commands, MI-96's menu half is VERIFIED. If it is still empty, the remaining candidate is CLIENT-SIDE CACHING and no code change reaches it -- but both code-side causes are now eliminated by evidence.
what_the_queue_learned_2026_09_03: ⚠️ 'ONLY POSITION 1 REBASES' IS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT, and the protocol above does not state the missing half. MEASURED THREE TIMES today on three different PRs (#10920, #10933, #10895), each on the same commit pair both ways: WITH the row-aware merge driver `git merge-tree --write-tree` returns CLEAN; WITHOUT it — which is what GitHub's servers run — the same pair CONFLICTS. A merge driver is CLIENT-SIDE. So a register-only conflict is locally trivial and PERMANENTLY un-mergeable server-side, and update_pull_request_branch refuses it outright. THE QUEUE THEREFORE ALSO NEEDS SOMEONE WITH AN ARMED CLONE AT EVERY STEP. Not a nicety: all three PRs had IDLE authors, an idle cloud session cannot be messaged, and none of them could have freed itself. It is also why MI-103's seven reconcile-open-prs PRs cannot self-heal. ⚠️ AND IT CORRECTS MI-20: the manager-only-PR pattern never worked because the conflict surface was empty — it is not, sub-sessions write MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json too and it genuinely conflicted today. It worked because the DRIVER resolves row-level register conflicts.
